name: Volt Active Data (VoltDB)
tagline: In-memory, partitioned SQL engine running Java stored procedures serially for millisecond decisioning.
description: Volt Active Data, the product formerly known as VoltDB, is an in-memory distributed SQL database that descends from the H-Store research project led by Michael Stonebraker. Data is partitioned across CPU cores, and each partition executes stored procedures serially, which avoids locking and delivers ACID transactions with predictable single-digit-millisecond latency at very high throughput. Snapshots and command logging provide durability, and import/export connectors plus topics connect it to Kafka-style streams. Today it is sold as a commercial real-time decisioning platform, mainly to telecom (charging, policy) and fraud-prevention customers. The open-source community edition stopped receiving updates in 2022.

pricing.notes: Commercial subscriptions; trial licenses available; deployable via Google Cloud Marketplace on GKE.

scale.notes: Data must fit in cluster RAM; scales by adding nodes and partitions; cross-datacenter replication (XDCR) supports active-active.

strengths: Serial execution per partition gives ACID with no locks or latches
Predictable single-digit-millisecond latency at millions of transactions per second
Java stored procedures keep decision logic next to the data
Built-in import/export and topics for streaming pipelines
weaknesses: Entire dataset must fit in memory
Multi-partition transactions are much slower than single-partition ones
Commercial-only; open-source edition is frozen since 2022
Small community and limited ecosystem tooling
useCases: Telecom online charging and policy control
Ad bidding and personalization at high TPS
notIdealFor: Teams wanting an open-source or managed-cloud option
